films.title: Gary's workday
films.premise: Owners say their dog had a busy day. Gary's day, logged like a job, is four kinds of lying down, and Doug knows it.
films.observation: owners describe a dog's day as busy
films.cruel: his coworker has seen the timesheet
films.caption: He says it was a long day.
films.music: mellow office lounge music, soft electric piano and brushed drums, easy and slightly smug, instrumental, no vocals

films.title: Doug copies Gary
films.premise: The younger dog copies everything the older one does, until the older one starts acting like he is under surveillance.
films.observation: a second dog copies the first
films.cruel: Gary is being watched in his own home
films.caption: Gary would like some privacy.
films.music: sneaky spy surveillance theme, pizzicato strings and muted trumpet, tiptoeing, instrumental, no vocals

films.title: The walk he begged for
films.premise: The dog begs for a walk and lies down two minutes in, but rides in the car anywhere, happily, without a single question.
films.observation: dogs beg for walks and then refuse to walk
films.stupid: the car is the walk he wanted
films.cruel: he never asks where the car is going
labels: The car, going who knows where.
films.caption: He has strong opinions about walking.
films.music: slow mournful solo cello for five seconds, then a bright sunny acoustic guitar road-trip groove, instrumental, no vocals

films.title: Leave it
films.premise: We taught him leave it, and he did, by lying on it.
films.cruel: the treat is still right there between his paws, and he dares you to ask
films.caption: Technically a good boy.
films.music: tense jazzy heist theme, walking double bass and snare brushes, sly, instrumental, no vocals

films.title: Best-trained dog (recut)
films.premise: The owner is proud the doodle was trained to wait before eating; the terrier was not, and is eating his dinner.
films.observation: owners brag about training a dog to wait at its bowl
films.cruel: the praise lands on the trained dog's sorrowful stare while the other one eats
labels: We trained him to wait before he eats.
films.caption: Patience is a virtue. Gary disagrees.
films.music: pompous proud brass marching band, ceremonial, instrumental, no vocals

films.title: Technically on the floor
films.premise: House rule: no dogs on the sofa. Doug keeps one paw on the floor, and Gary checks.
films.stupid: one paw on the floor counts as the floor
films.cruel: Gary, who follows the rule, is the one left on the rug
labels: House rule: no dogs on the sofa.
Doug is technically on the floor.
films.caption: The rule did not say how much of the dog.
films.music: light game show thinking music with a ticking clock, playful, instrumental, no vocals

films.title: Your alarm
films.premise: Your alarm goes off; the dog watches you, decides it was for you, and goes back to sleep.
films.observation: the dog stays in bed when you get up
films.stupid: the alarm only applies to you
films.cruel: he closes his eyes on you
labels: He has decided it was for you.
films.caption: Five more minutes, for him.
films.music: soft sleepy music box lullaby, gentle, instrumental, no vocals

music_only.title: Customs
music_only.music: tense airport customs inspection drone, low strings and a single ticking pulse, deadpan, instrumental, no vocals
